The draw call for the DynamicShadowOccluder / LiveStencilShadow path. Walks
the model-instance array (PTR_DAT_008b7da0, count/index list at +0x933c4/
+0x933c8), and for each instance with a byte flag at +0x140 set (role
unread) and the shadow.stencilvolume flag bit (self+0xe4 & 2) set, runs:

  SET_COLOR_MASK(0,0,0,0)                                    // color off
  Shadow_AccumulateStencilVolume(instance+0x128, ctx, ...)   // stencil write
  SET_COLOR_MASK(1,1,1,0)                                    // RGB on, alpha off
  <FUN_004053e0, not renamed - blend-enabled, alpha-tested draw>
  SET_COLOR_MASK(0,0,0,0)                                    // color off
  Shadow_ClearStencilVolume(instance+0x128, ctx, ...)        // stencil test + reset

FUN_004053e0 is bracketed by color-mask toggles the same way the two stencil
passes are, and is the only one of the three with color writes on and
alpha blending enabled (SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) - confirmed via
FUN_005c2380 = SET_COLOR_MASK (register 0x324) against a vendored rpcs3's
gcm_enums.h. That makes it the strongest candidate for the actual visible
darkening draw, not (as an earlier pass here guessed without checking) "the
caster's own regular mesh" - what geometry it actually submits is still
unconfirmed. instance+0x128 is a Resource_FindOrLoadByHashedPath handle
whose geometry Shadow_ParseStencilVolumeGeometry parses into an n-vertex/
m-u32-index pair (Shadow_AllocateStencilVolumeBuffers, closed by an exact
arithmetic invariant on the index width); m is the count both stencil passes
actually draw. See shadow-stencilvolume.md.

First of the two-pass stencil shadow volume: the depth-fail ("Carmack's
Reverse") stencil-write pass, color writes off (caller sets
SET_COLOR_MASK(0,0,0,0) immediately before). Confirmed against the vendored
rpcs3 source (Emu/RSX/gcm_enums.h) rather than assumed from general OpenGL
knowledge:

  Rsx_SetMethod(ctx, 0x183c, 0)   // NV4097_SET_CULL_FACE_ENABLE = off (draw both faces)
  Rsx_SetMethod(ctx, 0x328, 1)    // NV4097_SET_STENCIL_TEST_ENABLE = on
  Rsx_SetMethod(ctx, 0x348, 1)    // NV4097_SET_TWO_SIDED_STENCIL_TEST_ENABLE = on
  stencil func = ALWAYS (0x207), ref 1, mask 0xff, both faces
  stencil op = (KEEP, DECR_WRAP, KEEP) / (KEEP, INCR_WRAP, KEEP), front/back

(Rsx_UploadVertexConstants, using the technique object cached at
PTR_DAT_008bf4c4 - see Shader_ResolveLiveStencilShadowConstants), then draws
param_1 (the model instance's +0x128 handle from
Resource_FindOrLoadByHashedPath/Shadow_ParseStencilVolumeGeometry) via

TRIANGLE_STRIP (which is 6, GCM's list being 1-based unlike OpenGL's) -
walking a vector of 16-byte entries at param_1[2] (a std::vector-shaped
push_back target inside Shadow_ParseStencilVolumeGeometry, one entry per
parsed block: {index-buffer ptr, vertex-buffer ptr, u32 index count, vertex
count}), reading each entry's index count (offset +8) as the draw's index
count (108 for the real files - 36 triangles).

Checked 2026-09-04 against LiveStencilShadow_vp's own disassembly
(scripts/ps3-microcode.py, SHO block 0x00929600): the vertex program shifts
EVERY vertex by the same lightDirection*extrusionDistance, unconditionally -
not a per-vertex silhouette extrusion. This function's own vertex-constant
upload is a single call, computed from PTR_DAT_008bf4c4 the same way
Shadow_ClearStencilVolume computes it - neither function varies
extrusionDistance, so the two stencil passes submit the SAME once-shifted
closed box, not a near-cap/far-cap pair. The technique is closer to "does
this pixel's depth sample fall inside a fixed box template, shifted toward
the light and positioned at the caster" than a true silhouette-derived
shadow volume - still a legitimate two-sided depth-fail stencil test, just
built from a rigidly-shifted closed solid rather than an extruded one.

A real 39-file check (2026-09-04) of the geometry itself found 24 of the
box's 36 triangles are degenerate (zero-area - two of three vertices
coincide), on every file. Put together with the dead dot(normal,
lightDirection) this vertex program computes and never reads: 12 real face
triangles + 24 corner-bridging triangles is exactly the topology a true
near-cap/side-wall silhouette-extrusion volume needs, and dot(normal, light)
is exactly the term such a shader would need to decide which corner copies
to displace. Leading hypothesis, not confirmed: this asset and shader were
authored for a real silhouette extrusion, and the shipped vertex program
does not take that branch - it shifts every vertex uniformly instead,
leaving both the dead dot product and the degenerate triangles as vestiges.

Allocates the two GPU buffers Shadow_ParseStencilVolumeGeometry needs per
outer block, and closes the n/m question left open in the earlier pass:

  FUN_005a88c8(dest, n, 0x18, 2, ...)   // vertex buffer: n elements, 24-byte stride
  FUN_005a8750(dest, 0, m, ...)         // index buffer: m elements

Stores {index-buffer ptr, vertex-buffer ptr, m, n} into the caller's scratch
object (param_1[0..3]), which is exactly the 16-byte layout
Shadow_AccumulateStencilVolume/Shadow_ClearStencilVolume read per vector
entry - entry+8 (=m) is the count argument their draw call passes to
FUN_005a3e58. So **n sizes the vertex buffer (24-byte stride, matching the
geometry-record loop) and m sizes the index buffer and is the actual drawn
count**.

**Closed by an exact arithmetic invariant, 2026-09-04**: FUN_005a8750's own
branchless index-width computation, evaluated for the literal `param_2=0`
this call site passes, is `((0^0^0x10)-0-1)>>31 & 0xfffffffe) + 4 = 4` -
4-byte (u32) indices - and Shadow_ParseStencilVolumeGeometry's own memcpy of
the index blob is `m << 2` bytes, i.e. exactly `m` u32s. Two independently
read functions agreeing on the same byte size is the strongest evidence on
this page short of a runtime trace or a real file (confidence rubric's
85-94 band). FUN_005a88c8/FUN_005a8750 are generic buffer constructors
(confirmed by reading both - neither is shadow-specific, not renamed).

on (mode, sub): (1, 0xffff) registers both shaders and the IN_position/
IN_normal vertex attributes; (0, 0xffff) releases the previous technique's
refcounted resources. Called only from the two trampolines
Shader_ConstructLiveStencilShadowTechnique (mode=1) and
Shader_DestructLiveStencilShadowTechnique (mode=0) - a static object's
ctor/dtor pair, not a per-model call. Confidence 80.

Parses one shadow.stencilvolume resource buffer (param_2) into the
destination object (param_1, a 64-byte block allocated by
Resource_FindOrLoadByHashedPath). Confirmed field layout on param_1:
offset 0x0 = outer repeat-count (copied from param_2's own first u32);
0x8/0xc/0x10 = a std::vector's begin/end/capacity pointers (push_back idiom,
FUN_00734bd0 the grow-on-full helper); 0x20/0x30 = a running min/max
reduction over three of the six per-record floats (NOT a bounding box - see
below).

Per outer iteration: two u32 header fields (n, m - not u16), a third unread
header word, then Shadow_AllocateStencilVolumeBuffers(scratch, n, m)
allocates an n-vertex (24-byte stride) buffer and an m-index (u32) buffer -
see its own comment, which closes n/m's roles with an exact arithmetic
invariant. Then (n>0) a loop of n 24-byte/6-float input records is
copied/transformed into the new vertex buffer (the copy loop's exact
per-float source/dest mapping is heavily vectorized and decompiler-mangled,
not confidently traced); three of the six floats (byte offsets 0xc/0x10/0x14)
also feed the min/max reduction at param_1+0x20/+0x30. Byte-verified against
39/39 real shadow.stencilvolume PSARC entries (2026-09-04): the record is
(x,y,z,nx,ny,nz), so offsets 0xc/0x10/0x14 are a unit face NORMAL, not a
position - a min/max over normals in a fixed six-face box is a constant,
not a spatial bound, so param_1+0x20/+0x30's actual purpose is unresolved,
not "bbox" as an earlier pass here claimed. After the n records, an m*4-byte
index blob is memcpy'd into the new index buffer - matching
Shadow_AllocateStencilVolumeBuffers's own u32-index computation exactly.
One 16-byte {index-buf ptr, vertex-buf ptr, m, n} entry is then push_back'd
onto the vector at offset 0x8 - one entry per outer iteration, not per
n-record. The draw call (Shadow_AccumulateStencilVolume/
Shadow_ClearStencilVolume) walks this vector, reading each entry's m field
as its primitive count.

The 39/39 real files all share one exact header (n=24, m=108) and the same
topology: 24 vertices as 4 per face x 6 axis-aligned faces (an unwelded box),
108 indices as 12 face-quad triangles + 24 edge-bridging triangles sealing
it into one closed manifold. Only vertex positions vary per file (per-ship
bounding footprint) - the topology itself is byte-identical across every
file. This is the same coarse shape as Pulse's DynamicShadowOccluder .vex
payload (leading counts, a geometry array) but a different topology
encoding: HD pairs an explicit vertex buffer with an index buffer, where
Pulse's n (faces) and m (vertex slots) each index their own same-shaped
record array with no separate index list.
